text: What was the primary reason for the commercialisation of Indian agriculture?
options: The introduction of the Railways
The growth of urban centres and the demand for food grains
The expansion of the textile industry
The decline of the handicraft industry
correctAnswer: The growth of urban centres and the demand for food grains
explanation: The growth of urban centres and the demand for food grains led to the commercialisation of Indian agriculture. As the population shifted from rural to urban areas, the demand for food grains increased, prompting farmers to shift from subsistence farming to commercial farming to meet this demand.
subject: Economics
chapter: Ch 6: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence

text: What was the impact of the Railways on Indian agriculture?
options: It led to the commercialisation of Indian agriculture
It led to the decline of Indian agriculture
It had no impact on Indian agriculture
It led to the growth of the textile industry
correctAnswer: It led to the commercialisation of Indian agriculture
explanation: The Railways played a crucial role in the commercialisation of Indian agriculture. It enabled the transportation of food grains from rural areas to urban centres, leading to an increase in the demand for food grains and prompting farmers to shift from subsistence farming to commercial farming.
